topology_reasoning.device_identification: Symmetric two-waveguide directional coupler. The black material consists of two parallel input/output buses whose centerlines adiabatically move toward each other, run through a central close-gap interaction region, and separate again.
topology_reasoning.working_principle: Optical power transfer is set by the supermode splitting of the two close waveguides and by the physical interaction length. The S-bend access sections set adiabatic approach/separation and port pitch while the central gap and coupling length define the transfer ratio.
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Use gf.Path centerlines extruded on layer (1,0). The two guides are mirrored about the footprint midline; each centerline uses straight leads, smoothstep S-bend transitions, and a straight coupled section. No component stencils or raw polygons are used.

iterations.change_made: Initial fitted primitives-only directional coupler: two gf.Path centerlines extruded on layer (1,0), using calibrated median guide width, fitted port/coupled separations, smoothstep S-bend transitions, and central coupling length. Diff showed only thin edge residuals, so this was kept as best.

knob_verification.rationale: One-guide interaction/phase-length trim compatible with the verifier's one-guide area-growth contract; image-defining coupler knobs remain top-level tunables.
